newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Congress sees minority Pequiven sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Congress sees minority Pequiven sell-off.

text.p: The Venezuelan government would keep a majority stake in the state petrochemical company Pequiven according to a privatisation plan being discussed by Congress, a Deputy who proposed the plan said on Wednesday.
Wednesday's was only the first of four debates before Congress is due to vote on the law and sources say it could still undergo changes.

Ramon Jose Medina, one of the Deputies who proposed the new law, said, "Pequiven would remain a state company, a company with mixed ownership where there is private participation but where the state keeps a majority of the shares."
Earlier this year, Pequiven president Arnold Volkenborn said he wanted to see a majority stake in private hands.

"I don't see a long line of investors queueing up for a minority stake of a company controlled by the government," said a Venezuelan banking source. "If they go ahead with this plan, they will have to make some concessions on control," he added.

Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta, presenting the plan to Congress on Wednesday, asked Deputies to vote in favour. He said it was vital to increase Pequiven's access to private capital to fund an aggressive expansion strategy.

Pequiven plans $5.9 billion in investment over the next ten years, increasing output from 7.7 million tonnes to 18.4 million tonnes per year, he said. Venezuela's cheap supply of gas feedstock and location close to large consuming markets gave it competitive advantage, although Trinidad, Chile, Brazil, Argentina and Colombia were all competing for petrochemical investment dollars.
